claims.text: This is the only paper in our selection that explicitly focuses on mid-training as its primary research question.
The authors investigate how mid-training strategies shape reinforcement learning dynamics across Qwen and Llama model families.

Key findings include: (1) high-quality mathematical corpora significantly improve both base model and RL performance, (2) adding QA-style data with long chain-of-thought reasoning examples enhances RL outcomes, (3) long-CoT can induce verbosity and training instability, highlighting the importance of data formatting, and (4) scaling mid-training consistently leads to stronger downstream RL performance.

The authors introduce a two-stage "Stable-then-Decay" mid-training strategy: first training on 200B tokens with constant learning rate, followed by 20B tokens across three CoT-focused branches with learning rate decay.
This approach yields OctoThinker models with strong RL compatibility.
This paper demonstrates mid-training through continued pre-training of DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B with 120B math-related tokens.
The approach combines mathematical data sourced from Common Crawl with natural language and code data.
DeepSeekMath 7B achieved 51.7% on the MATH benchmark without external toolkits, approaching Gemini-Ultra and GPT-4 performance.

The success is attributed to: (1) a meticulously engineered data selection pipeline harnessing publicly available web data, and (2) Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) enhancing mathematical reasoning while optimizing PPO memory usage.
LLaMAX employs extensive multilingual continual pre-training on LLaMA series models to support translation across 100+ languages.
The mid-training strategy includes vocabulary expansion and data augmentation without sacrificing generalization ability.

LLaMAX achieves significantly higher translation performance (10+ spBLEU points) compared to existing open-source LLMs and performs on-par with specialized translation model M2M-100-12B on Flores-101 benchmark.
Tower employs continued pretraining on a multilingual mixture of monolingual and parallel data (TowerBase), followed by finetuning on translation-relevant instructions (TowerInstruct).
This two-stage mid-training approach creates models that surpass open alternatives on translation workflow tasks and compete with closed general-purpose LLMs.
The authors release the specialization dataset, evaluation framework, and model generations.
Qwen3 represents a comprehensive series employing sophisticated multi-stage training.
The approach includes scaled pre-training datasets (18 trillion tokens vs. 7 trillion in Qwen2.5), intricate supervised finetuning with 1M+ samples, and multistage reinforcement learning.
Qwen3 introduces unified thinking/non-thinking modes and a thinking budget mechanism.

The series spans 0.6B to 235B parameters in both dense and MoE architectures, achieving state-of-the-art results in code generation, mathematical reasoning, and agent tasks while expanding multilingual support from 29 to 119 languages.
Qwen2.5 demonstrates significant improvements through enhanced pre-training and post-training stages.
Pre-training scaled from 7T to 18T tokens, providing strong foundations for common sense, expert knowledge, and reasoning.

Post-training implements intricate supervised finetuning with 1M+ samples and multistage reinforcement learning, enhancing human preference alignment, long text generation, structural data analysis, and instruction following.
The flagship Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct performs competitively with Llama-3-405B-Instruct despite being 5× smaller.

SmolLM2 demonstrates that small models (1.7B parameters) can achieve strong performance through overtraining on ~11T tokens using multi-stage training mixing web text with specialized math, code, and instruction-following data.
The authors introduce new specialized datasets (FineMath, Stack-Edu, SmolTalk) and employ a manual refinement process updating dataset mixing rates at each stage based on previous performance.
This data-centric mid-training approach enables SmolLM2 to outperform Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama3.2-1B.
Magicoder introduces OSS-Instruct, a novel approach using open-source code snippets to generate diverse instruction data for code mid-training.
Training on 75K synthetic instruction data mitigates LLM bias through open-source references, producing more realistic and controllable data.
MagicoderS-CL-7B (based on CodeLlama) surpasses ChatGPT on HumanEval+ (66.5 vs. 65.9 pass@1), demonstrating the effectiveness of this mid-training data generation approach.
MATES introduces model-aware data selection where a data influence model continuously adapts to evolving data preferences during pretraining.
Unlike static methods, MATES collects oracle data influence by locally probing the pretraining model and fine-tunes a small influence model to approximate it.
The influence model predicts data influence over the entire corpus and selects the most influential data for each pretraining stage.
Experiments show MATES significantly outperforms random selection, doubling gains from state-of-the-art reference model approaches and reducing total FLOPs by half to reach target performance.
REWIRE (REcycling the Web with guIded REwrite) addresses the "data wall" in pre-training scaling by transforming and recycling data discarded in filtering processes.
The method enriches low-quality documents to make them useful for training, increasing synthetic data representation.

Experiments at 1B, 3B, and 7B scales show mixing high-quality raw texts with rewritten texts improves performance by 1.0, 1.3, and 2.5 percentage points across 22 tasks compared to filtered web data alone.
Training on raw-synthetic mixes outperforms having 2× web data, with 82% of mixed data coming from transformed low-quality documents.

Format Matters: Wang et al. (2025) highlight that data formatting, particularly for chain-of-thought reasoning, critically impacts training stability and downstream performance, suggesting mid-training requires attention beyond content selection.
RL Compatibility: Further investigation into mid-training strategies that optimize for reinforcement learning scalability, as initiated by Wang et al. (2025).

While OctoThinker (Wang et al., 2025) provides the only explicit mid-training framework, the widespread adoption of mid-training techniques across all reviewed papers indicates its centrality to modern LLM development.
